texts:
One photo of a garden gnome went in, and a textured 3D model came out, built in the browser with the garden cut away: three.ws/image-to-3d

It is free, with no sign-up and no API key. The free engines run on NVIDIA-hosted generation and our own self-hosted GPU workers, so the machine you upload from needs no GPU of its own. When the model lands, orbit it and download the GLB.

One photo leaves the back of the object to the model to guess. Photo mode takes up to 6 views of the same object and reconstructs them together, so a second or third angle replaces the guess with what is actually there.

The reel uses a single public domain photo, and the wait for the model is cut and labelled on screen.

The result is a GLB you keep. From the same screen you can view it in AR in your own room, split it into selectable parts, or retopologize it to a poly budget and export an engine-ready GLB and FBX.

Agents get it too: the same pipeline is available to agents over MCP, so a bot can turn a photo into a model without opening the page.

One photo of a garden gnome went in, and a textured 3D model came out, built in the browser with the garden cut away: three.ws/image-to-3d

It is free, with no sign-up and no API key. The free engines run on NVIDIA-hosted generation and our own self-hosted GPU workers, so the machine you upload from needs no GPU of its own. When the model lands, orbit it and download the GLB.

One photo leaves the back of the object to the model to guess. Photo mode takes up to 6 views of the same object and reconstructs them together, so a second or third angle replaces the guess with what the camera saw.

The reel uses a single public domain photo, and the wait for the model is cut and labelled on screen.

The result is a GLB you keep, downloaded from the same screen you made it on.

Agents get it too: the same pipeline is available to agents over MCP, so a bot can turn a photo into a model without opening the page.

editor.summary: Posts 1 and 2 are accurate and on-voice, but post 3 makes three feature claims (AR in your room, split into selectable parts, retopologize with GLB and FBX export) whose verification against the live page failed, so they are removed in the rewrite. Also fix the 5.2 s caption that calls a wireframe a textured model, replace the filler "actually", and re-run the scenario probe that timed out before scheduling.
